stories.title: O'Neill asked to attend PSNI interview over protests
stories.summary: Sinn Féin deputy leader and Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O’Neill has received a letter from the PSNI asking her to attend a voluntary interview under caution in connection with protests on the Garvaghy Road in Portadown. Party leader Mary Lou McDonald has said she also expects to receive a letter. In a statement, Ms O'Neill said she will co-operate with the investigation. "I can confirm I have received a letter inviting me for a police interview in relation to a peaceful protest on the Garvaghy Road. I will co-operate with the investigation. "For the last two weeks, I have stood in solidarity with the Garvaghy Road residents as attempts were made to force an unwanted Orange march through their community. "I will continue to stand with the Garvaghy Road residents who should be allowed to live in peace and free from sectarian intimidation.

stories.title: Job openings down 4.8% in third quarter - Morgan McKinley
stories.summary: Job openings across Ireland were down on an annual basis by 4.8% in the third quarter of the year, according to the latest employment monitor from recruitment firm Morgan McKinley. The research also showed that vacancies are up slightly, by 0.2%, on the previous quarter. Jobseeker registrations rose sharply, up 14% quarter on quarter, and 51% year-on-year. However, according to the report, the increase in jobseeker registrations does not correspond with a rise in unemployment meaning that many workers are exploring opportunities while staying in their current roles. The research found that artificial intelligence is reshaping recruitment, with employers expecting practical AI capability across finance, human resources, marketing and operations. Businesses are also managing a rise in AI-assisted applications, AI-generated CVs and concerns around candidate authenticity.

stories.title: Polanski vows to stay Greens leader despite election loss
stories.summary: Zack Polanski has insisted he will carry on as Greens leader despite failing to win a seat in Parliament as the fallout continued from the party conference backing a motion declaring Zionism is racism. The UK Green Party leader's position was being questioned by senior colleagues even before he was unsuccessful in ousting Labour in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election triggered by the resignation of former prime minister Keir Starmer. Mr Polanski said "of course I can carry on" as party leader but acknowledged that ultimately Green members would decide his fate. He was defeated by Camden Council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali, who retained the north London seat for Labour. She secured 45% of the vote to the Greens' 33%, a majority of 3,364 but seeing a 13% swing to the Greens, whose vote share was up by 22.4%. Mr Polanski missed the Green Party conference vote which endorsed a policy effectively calling for Israel to be abolished and replaced with a single Palestinian state.

stories.title: DCC Energy to sell tech unit Nexora for $725m
stories.summary: Energy distributor DCC Energy said today it would sell its technology division, Nexora, to private equity firm One Equity Partners for a total enterprise value of $725m on a cash- and debt-free basis. The sale of the business is expected to complete on or after March 1, 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, DCC said in a statement. DCC agreed to a £5.75 billion takeover by a consortium of US private equity firms KKR and Energy Capital Partners in July. DCC said its shareholders will receive an additional 42 pence per share on top of the existing offer from the KKR-led consortium. But if regulatory conditions related to the sale of Nexora are not met by July 31, 2027, the additional consideration will be zero, it added. Donal Murphy, the chief executive of DCC Energy, said Nexora has been an important part of the DCC Group for many years and has built a strong market position through the expertise and commitment of its people.

stories.title: France students plan more protests as UN voice 'concern'
stories.summary: Students in France were largely back in the classroom today following days of protests demanding better education and school conditions, as the UN voiced "concern" over the sometimes-violent clashes. Tens of thousands have taken to the streets across France since students in late September began blocking entrances to high schools, which led to squads of riot police being deployed. The students - most aged 15 to 18 - have complained of absent teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that cannot cope with rising temperatures. More than 6,800 people have been detained since the start of the demonstrations, of whom 86% are minors, the justice ministry said today. A government source told journalists that the cost for damage caused by the demonstrations was "at least €30 million". The United Nations said today that it was watching the events "with concern" and urged people on all sides to remain peaceful.

stories.title: Ward hails 'outstanding' Ireland after Astana cakewalk
stories.summary: Republic of Ireland boss Carla Ward's praised her side's professionalism after they overwhelmed Kazakhstan in the first leg of the World Cup play-off semi-final on Friday. The Girls in Green cruised to an 8-0 win that ends the tie as a contest. The countries meet in the return leg at SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh on Tuesday, but there'll be little competitive edge to that fixture. Ireland can't be blamed for that of course. It was a job well done for Ward's team who are 77 places higher than the Kazakhs in the world rankings and were heavy favourites to prevail even without star pair Katie McCabe (suspended) and Denise O'Sullivan (rested). "The girls deserve an awful lot of credit, because we spoke all week about no complacency, making sure we do the job professionally, making sure we have the same approach as if we were playing some of the best in the world. They did that and I thought they were outstanding. "It's tough to come to a place like this and play against a team that sit behind the ball in the manner in which they did, so I think the girls deserve an awful lot of credit." McCabe, O'Sullivan, Marissa Sheva and Jess Ziu could all return for the game in Cork, further intensifying competition for places.

stories.title: Interviews begin as Monaghan seek new boss
stories.summary: Monaghan GAA are set to meet on Friday night as the search for their new manager intensifies with a number of candidates already interviewed. Louth manager Gavin Devlin was another potential name on the radar but he reaffirmed his commitment to the Wee County for 2027. Enda McGinley likewise is focused on Errigal Ciarán as they chase a Tyrone title. Armagh man John McEntee has spent the last four seasons with Inniskeen and in his opening campaign took the club to their first Monaghan final since 1990 and repeated the trick in 2025. In the other two seasons he brought the club to the semi-finals. On all four occasions, their season was brought to an end by Ulster champions Scotstown, who won a thrilling semi-final at Clones on Sunday afternoon. McEntee's interview comes seven years after twin brother Tony went for the same role, but was beaten to it by Séamus McEnaney who began his second stint with the Oriel County. Andy McEntee spent last season in the Monaghan camp after being brought on board by Bannigan after Andy Moran’s move to Mayo.

stories.title: Ireland U21s poised to learn Euro 2027 play-off opponents
stories.summary: The Republic of Ireland Under-21s will learn who they have to beat to secure their place at the 2027 European Championship on Friday. Jim Crawford's side are in the pot for the play-off draw which takes place in Nyon at 10am. Ireland secured their place in the play-offs with a stunning 3-1 victory over England at Turner's Cross to finish runners-up in Group D and edge out Slovakia, who finished third and miss out on the draw. Trailing to an eighth-minute goal by Tyler Dibling, Ireland roared back with two goals from Tommy Lonergan and another from Conor McManus to book their place in the eight-country play-offs. The play-off draw is an open one and will not be seeded, meaning that Ireland can play any of the other seven teams in the draw. Czechia, Denmark, Finland, Greece, Iceland, Netherlands and Turkey are all potential opponents for the Boys in Green.

stories.title: URC teams: Provinces welcome back internationals for R3
stories.summary: The Irish provinces have welcomed back a host of their international frontline stars, ahead of this weekend's Round 3 games in the BKT United Rugby Championship. Ulster and Munster's Interpro in Belfast is the marquee game of the weekend on Saturday night, with Tadhg Beirne back in to captain Munster at Affidea Stadium, while Ulster head coach Richie Murphy has been able to recall Nick Timoney, Stuart McCloskey, Jacob Stockdale and Rob Baloucoune for their first games of the season. It's the same front row that started against Glasgow, with Eric O’Sullivan, Tom Stewart and former Munster man Keynan Knox packing down, with Ben Donnell joining Eli Snyman in the second row. Cormac Izuchukwu shifts to flanker, with Timoney and Juarno Augustus both coming in to form a new back row, replacing James McKillop, David McCann and the injured Bryn Ward. Nathan Doak starts his first game of the season at scrum-half, and Matthew Devine is named on the bench, having been an injury concern this week. Jack Murphy continues in the 10 shirt, with McCloskey coming in for Ben Carson at centre, and Jamie Benson pivoting to the 13 shirt.

stories.title: Dream big - inside The Ark's new anthology of plays for kids
stories.summary: Aideen Howard, creative director of The Ark, introduces Dream Big, the new book collecting a quintet of original (and acclaimed) theatre works commissioned by the children's cultural centre. As a young drama student in 1995, I remember vividly the excitement surrounding the opening of Europe's first ever dedicated children cultural centre. That this ground-breaking innovation was happening in the heart of Dublin city was a source of pride. The Ark Children’s Cultural Centre opened its doors in Temple Bar, three years after the Irish government ratified the United Nations Convention on the Rights of The Child which recognised the right of children to 'participate freely in cultural life and the arts.’ History was being made. Ireland was showing a new cultural confidence in its vision for investment in both the arts and children. Now, thirty years after its founding, over a million children and their parents and teachers have attended The Ark. Our purpose is to realise children’s right to art and culture with ambition and joy. We do so by commissioning, producing and presenting new art for, by, with and about children from birth to age 12. From the beginning I was inspired by The Ark’s radical approach to art making and community engagement. When I was appointed Director in 2015, I was keen to build on those strong foundations. One of my first projects was to introduce a child participation practice to redistribute decision making power across the organisation alongside a new commissioning strategy. The Ark Children’s Council was established and now plays a key role in all decision-making and inform the development of every new commission. The five writers featured in Dream Big have created new worlds of the imagination.

stories.title: Irish designer Sasha Donnellan on finding her calling in Paris
stories.summary: Ellen Corcoran meets with Sasha Donnellan, the Irish designer who has captivated celebrity clients like Laura Whitmore and Roz Purcell, ahead of a dazzling presentation of her work during Paris Fashion Week. In the foyer of Hôtel Le Marois, I meet an elated and energetic Sasha Donnellan. She has a suitcase full of garments to bring back to Ireland ahead of her Ireland Fashion Week show in Dublin on Sunday morning, where she will showcase her full 20-look collection. The crowd finally fizzles out of the building and we find a seat by a grand piano as she catches her breath. Just 15 minutes earlier, a glimpse of her brand new collection, 'The Calling', had graced the runway for the very first time as part of Flying Solo NYC’s Paris Fashion Week show. Naturally, I ask how she’s feeling. "I was very nervous, of course, but also excited to see how people would perceive it, because I think this collection is quite different to my previous work", she says. "I feel like previous collections were much more focused on silks, and this time, I really leaned into my outerwear interest. That's something I haven't done before. So I was excited to see how people would react." Sasha refers to each of her collections as "little chapters" of her life. "I’m a designer, I love storytelling. To me, each collection represents a chapter that reflects something I'm incredibly passionate about at that moment." This time, that meant exploring the idea of a calling. Following her hugely successful Ireland Fashion Week debut in 2025, Sasha made the decision to become independent and commit fully to working on her brand, a move that prompted her to think about the people throughout history who had followed their own sense of purpose.

stories.title: Man charged with Mike Gaine murder wants new barristers
stories.summary: A former US soldier charged with murdering Co Kerry sheep farmer Mike Gaine wants new barristers ahead of his nine-week trial next January, the Central Criminal Court has heard. Michael Kelley, a native of Maine in the US but of no fixed abode in Tralee, Co Kerry, was sent forward for trial in Dublin last May after being served with the book of evidence. Mr Kelley, 54, is charged with a single count of murdering Mr Gaine, 56, at Carrig, Kenmare, Co Kerry, on a date unknown between 20 and 21 March 2025. Mr Kelley is expected to go on trial at the Central Criminal Court on 11 January 2027. The court was previously told by counsel for the Director of Public Prosecutions that there are 191 witnesses in the book of evidence and it is estimated the case will last up to nine weeks. In a brief hearing before the Central Criminal Court today, defence counsel Brendan Grehan SC told Mr Justice Paul McDermott that he had been instructed by solicitor Mr Frank Buttimer on behalf of Mr Kelley, alongside Richard Liston BL.

stories.title: Independent TV producers concerned over RTÉ funding cut
stories.summary: "And certainly, I think removing €20 million from that commitment, or not standing by that commitment, is enormously concerning because, obviously, there's every likelihood that, as Kevin Bakhurst articulated, those pretty difficult decisions, the impact there is on the independent production sector, and it's on our audiences." The funding was expected to reach €260m for 2027 as part of the €725m three-year agreement but instead will stand at €240m, representing a decrease of €20m. Minister O'Donovan said the decrease was due to his dissatisfaction with what he called the broadcaster's progress in implementing promised reforms. In an email to staff on Wednesday, Mr Bakhurst said that this decision "is one we had not anticipated and will inevitably impact on our ability to deliver our five-year strategy". Screen Producers Ireland is a representative group of independent producers in the film and television industry in Ireland. Ms Kirby said its members are the makers of "everything from The Traitors to Normal People to An Cailín Ciúin to First Dates, Dancing with the Stars, The Lost Children of Tuam".

stories.title: Delta Air slashes profit forecast over fuel-cost surge
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines cut its annual profit forecast by nearly a quarter today as soaring fuel costs, expected to add $6 billion to its bill in 2026, overwhelmed resilient travel demand and higher ticket prices. Its shares fell 2.5% in early trading after the carrier cut its 2026 profit forecast for the first time this year and lifted its projected fuel-cost increase by $2 billion as the Iran war has driven jet fuel prices sharply higher worldwide. With no end to the war in sight, carriers are confronting their worst crisis since the pandemic. The downgrade underscores a growing challenge for the industry: whether passengers will absorb further fare increases if fuel prices remain elevated. Airlines have already raised fares substantially this year and analysts warn further increases could test travelers' willingness to keep spending. Delta, the first major global carrier to report third-quarter results, said fuel expenses for the period rose 62% from a year earlier to $4.1 billion, exceeding its July forecast by more than $500 million. "All of it's fuel," Delta Chief Financial Officer Erik Snell told reporters when asked what drove the forecast cut, citing increases in both crude oil and refined jet fuel prices since the summer. Delta now expects adjusted annual earnings of $5.10 to $5.60 a share, down from the $6.50 to $7.50 per share it forecast in July. The new midpoint of $5.35 per share is below analysts' average estimate of $5.46 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG. It forecast $4.5 billion in adjusted pre-tax profit for 2026.

stories.title: Pillay: From global rights activist to Nobel Prize winner
stories.summary: Nobel Peace Prize recipient Navi Pillay is a fearless global rights defender. The 85-year-old former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights also served on the International Criminal Court and the International Tribunal for Rwanda. She was also South Africa's first non-white woman High Court judge. Ms Pillay built a formidable reputation during a decades-long career. She gained global prominence for her outspoken condemnation of government repression of popular protests in the Arab world, including Libya and Syria. Between 2021 and 2025, she chaired a panel - created by the UN Human Rights Council - to investigate the root causes of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

stories.title: Wafer misses out as Bemand names squad for South Africa
stories.summary: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand has named a 30-player squad that will face South Africa in back-to-back WXV Global Series tests on 24 October and 31 October - with Aoife Wafer and Sam Monaghan ruled out due to injury. Wafer underwent surgery on an ankle injury while Monaghan suffered a knee injury while on duty for Gloucester-Hartpury in August. The games, coming after their home loss to USA and victories over Japan, will be played at the Athlone Stadium in Cape Town. Erin King will lead the 30-player travelling squad, with recently capped players Beth Buttimer, Jemima Adams Verling, Kate Jordan, Sophie Barrett and Alana McInerney all included. Second row Ruth Campbell returns from injury to travel with the squad but Monaghan and Wafer have been ruled out. After a remote training week following their recent victories over Japan in Galway and Cork, Ireland return to camp at the IRFU High Performance Centre on Monday before travelling to Cape Town on Thursday.

stories.title: Underdogs could get home advantage in new Leinster format
stories.summary: Leinster GAA chairperson Martin Byrne says the province will be open to the prospect of giving underdogs home advantage in knockout games under the council's proposed new championship structure. A motion to Congress 2027 is being drafted following Leinster GAA management approval with a view to forming an eight-team provincial SHC, which would be split into two groups of four. In that instance, Group 1 would comprise higher tier teams made up of the top four teams from the 2027 series. Group 2 would feature the fifth and sixth-placed teams from ’27, along with the two Joe McDonagh Cup finalists. Byrne revealed his council will remain open to the possibility of an underdog receiving home advantage in a knockout game. "Where venues come up in all of this will be decided by our CCCC (Central Competitions Control Committee) in 2028," he said.

stories.title: New Munster CEO keen for O'Mahony input
stories.summary: Munster's new interim chief executive says he has already reached out to former players, including Peter O’Mahony, ahead of taking the role of CEO this month. Avan Lee has been appointed by the province on an interim basis, replacing outgoing chief executive Ian Flanagan who is to step down at the end of October. The New Zealander, who spent 10 years running the Hurricanes in Super Rugby between 2015 and 2025, will initially be CEO on an interim basis, but has confirmed he would be interested in becoming the province's permanent chief. Flanagan’s position has been under scrutiny for several months following last season’s off-field turmoil, most notably the appointment of Roger Randle as attack coach, which was ultimately cancelled by both parties in April. Further pressure landed on the province last week form their former captain O’Mahony, whose stinging criticism of how Munster is run came just three days before Flanagan’s resignation. And speaking after his appointment yesterday, Lee said he has already been in touch with O’Mahony - among others – to get their opinions on where the province need to improve as an organisation.

stories.title: Open House Dublin - the festival of architecture returns
stories.summary: Emmett Scanlon, Director of the Irish Architecture Foundation, introduces the 2026 edition of Open House Dublin, the capital's festival of architecture, which returns this October. This year's Open House Festival explores the idea that "Dublin Is Living" and that people are its life support. On a daily basis, it is communities of place and interest, on streets, in rooms, parks and pitches, that form and shape Dublin city and county. This year we place this unique relationship between people and place front and centre at Ireland’s largest and longest running festival of architecture. Our nine-day festival invites you to explore the city and county and join a conversation about our capital's future. More than 200 free events are taking place, from behind-the-scenes tours to talks, workshops and exhibitions. People of all ages, backgrounds and abilities can discover Dublin and consider what it means to live, thrive and belong here. For younger visitors, Open House Junior brings architecture to life on 10–11 October with free workshops, walking tours and creative activities for children, teenagers and families to explore and reimagine the places around them. For the first time, our 'Open Table' series will take place across all four Dublin local authority areas. Hosted by housing and urban design expert Dr Lorcan Sirr, these lunchtime conversations are a chance to share experiences, local knowledge and ideas for their neighbourhoods. From 12-15 October, in Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown, Fingal, South Dublin and Dublin City, the discussions will feed into the Dublin Is Living Town Hall. Happening on the evening of Thursday 15 October at Wood Quay, the Dublin Is Living Town Hall will bring together residents, community advocates, local business owners and voices from architecture and public life to discuss the big questions facing Dublin, including housing, vacant buildings, transport, green space, safety and belonging. Perspectives gathered at the Open Tables will bring neighbourhood experiences into this wider discussion about Dublin’s future.

stories.title: Pat Ingoldsby to sparkle again on spoken-word album
stories.summary: One Good Sparkle, a spoken word album celebrating the life and poetry of the late Pat Ingoldsby, will be digitally released this Monday, with a CD version to follow. Imelda May is among those who will appear on the album, which came about after a funding campaign earlier this year by Athlone-based publishing house Luain Press. He hosted children's TV shows, wrote plays for the stage and radio, published books of short stories and poems and was a newspaper columnist. One Good Sparkle features 18 of Mr Ingoldsby's poems, with Words to the Virus Which Found Me in 1942, (read by the poet himself), the title track (read by Anna D.), and Da Down the Garden (read by Daragh Fleming) already released. The other poems on the album are read by spoken artists Mikey Cullen, Emmet O'Brien, Stephen Maguire, Leon Dunne, Jan Brierton, Stephen James Smith, Ryan Duggins, Lee Sheridan, Annie Peter, David Hynes, Steve O'Toole and Holly Hughes. The readings will be accompanied by music by Welsh pianist and composer Philip May.

stories.title: Why Irish designers are so drawn to the Gothic in fashion
stories.summary: Laura Fitzachary is a historian and historical content creator based in Dublin who specialises in fashion and beauty history in Ireland and beyond. Ahead of spooky season, fashion historian Laura Fitzachary explores how Gothic tropes and traditional Irish stories have Irish fashion designers enthralled. Inspired by storytelling and craftsmanship, Gothic fashion naturally finds a home in Ireland. So it is not surprising that Irish designers such as Jonathan Anderson, Dior Creative Director, and Simone Rocha have referenced Gothic literature, Irish mythology and Victorian mourning dress. A literal take on the iconic Dior Book Tote was revealed by Magherafelt-born Anderson in 2025 in the lead up Dior Homme SS '26, one of which featured an homage to the first edition of Dracula by Bram Stoker. As noted by Dior, Stoker’s Dracula take its place in Anderson’s "dream library". The Gothic horror novel was published in 1897 and draws extensively from folklore and history. While there are several theories as to who the character of 'Dracula’ is based on, this mystery has even spilled over into fashion. Alexander McQueen’s FW ‘09 Menswear featured models bearing a cane, a top hat and a coat draped over the shoulders – a direct nod to the human form of the vampire depicted by Gary Oldman in Bram Stoker’s Dracula, Francis Ford Coppola's 1992 interpretation of the novel. What is known is the strong influence of traditional Irish tales on Stoker’s writing, which has been argued by historians such as David J. Skal.

stories.title: Kickboxer threatened woman before killing mother - court
stories.summary: An amateur kickboxer suffering a drug-induced hallucination that he was Jesus Christ held a butcher's knife to a terrified grandmother's neck just five weeks before he killed his own mother, a court has heard. Luke Donnelly, aged 30, was sentenced at the Central Criminal Court in June to seven-and-a-half years in prison, with the final 12 months suspended, for the manslaughter of 62-year-old Catherine Henry in Dundalk, Co Louth, on 23 May 2023. He appeared at Mullingar Circuit Criminal Court, having entered guilty pleas to two offences which happened in the months before he fatally attacked Ms Henry. He admitted to aggravated burglary at a house at Grange Heights, Mullingar, Co Westmeath, while armed with a kitchen knife on 13 April 2023. Donnelly also pleaded guilty to assault causing harm to a man in his 20s at Delvin Road, Mullingar, on 8 August 2022. At the time of the offences, Donnelly lived in Riverbank, Drogheda, Co Louth, and Killucan, Co Westmeath, and had only one minor prior conviction.

stories.title: OpenAI sacks three safety researchers for breach of trust
stories.summary: OpenAI has said it has sacked three safety researchers for a "breach of trust", defending the dismissals after the trio accused the company of putting its corporate interests before safety as the reason for removing them. The ChatGPT maker said in a post on X that it "parted ways" with the researchers after an investigation found "they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information". The statement comes after the three researchers, Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni, posted a letter to OpenAI's various safety oversight groups detailing the circumstances around their sackings and their concerns about AI. The researchers said they feared that the "internal and external communications" about their dismissals have chilled the company's culture that encouraged speaking freely and disagreeing openly about safety concerns. They urged OpenAI to stick to its promise to allow third-party safety monitors inside the company and preserve the ability to monitor rapidly advancing frontier AI models that could pose unknown risks. Two other safety researchers and I were fired from OpenAI last week. We wrote this letter to leadership. I believe we were fired for prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation. https://t.co/ALANn9B87S

stories.title: Opposition TDs consider Dáil boycott over strike pickets
stories.summary: Doubt hangs over Wednesday's sitting of the Dáil amid a national day of strike action by public sector workers. Opposition TDs are considering boycotting the sitting should they be required to pass the picket of striking Oireachtas workers. More than 100,000 public sector workers are to take action next week despite a plea in Tuesday's budget speech by Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers to engage in dialogue about a new pay deal. In a note to TDs and senators last week, Clerk of the Dáil and Secretary General of the Houses of the Oireachtas Services Elaine Gunn said that Dáil and Seanad sittings, as well as committee hearings, could be affected by any action. It is understood the Houses of the Oireachtas is seeking a derogation to allow its staff to work on Wednesday and to facilitate sittings in both chambers, with a decision on whether it will be granted due tomorrow evening. However, a meeting of the Dáil's Committee on Business heard reservations from opposition TDs about proceeding with Oireachtas business should a derogation not be granted.

stories.title: 28% of new private cars licensed so far this year EVs
stories.summary: New figures from the Central Statistics Office show that new private electric cars licensed for the first time in September grew by 54% on the same time last year. The CSO said that 3,074 new private electric cars were licensed in September compared with 2,000 for the same month in 2025. Today's figures show that licensing of hybrid vehicles decreased by 2% from 1,217 in September last year to 1,197 new private cars in September of this year. But the number of new plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) licensed grew by 24% with 1,296 such vehicles licensed last month compared to 1,045 the same time last year. The CSO said the share of electric vehicles among new private cars from January to September rose to 28% compared with 19% for the same time in 2025. It added that the combined share of petrol and diesel cars among new private cars licensed so far this year fell to 31% from 43% in 2025.

stories.title: Three Saudi nationals killed in attacks on Riyadh airport
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has said three Saudi nationals, including a pilot, have been killed in attacks on Riyadh's international airport, after Yemen's Houthis claimed a series of attacks targeting the facility. The conflict between the Houthis and Yemen's Saudi-backed government has widened, with the Iran-backed fighters staging repeated attacks on Saudi targets since they began a lightning offensive just across the border. While seizing large swathes of territory along the Red Sea coast in Yemen, the Houthis have also attacked Saudi transport hubs, oil facilities and other civilian targets in the world's largest crude exporter. The Saudi civil aviation authority said two attacks yesterday on the Saudi capital's airport and a Saudia Airlines plane there "resulted in the martyrdom of three citizens". The national flag carrier confirmed the death of the plane's captain, expressing "profound sadness" and citing an "incident" at King Khalid International Airport. Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government forces it backs have struggled to contain the Houthis' advance, despite a counter-offensive aimed at recapturing territory including the area around the Bab al-Mandab strait that is crucial to global energy flows.

stories.title: Ireland pitted against Finland in Euro U21 play-offs
stories.summary: The Republic of Ireland U21s will play Finland for a place in at the place 2027 European Championships in Albania and Serbia. Jim Crawford's side were paired with the Finns for the play-off round at the draw in Nyom, Switzerland this morning and the Boys in Green will be relatively pleased with their opponents. Ireland avoided the Netherlands, Denmark and Czechia all of who are ranked higher than them in the UEFA Under-21 coefficient. Crawford's team are ranked 18th with the Finns in 20th, pointing to what looks like being an evenly match tie. The play-offs will be played over two legs between 13 and 17 November, and Ireland will be away for the first leg before playing the second leg at home. Ireland will be full of confidence heading into the play-off given how they secured their place in the draw with a stunning 3-1 victory over England at Turner's Cross to finish runners-up in Group D and edge out Slovakia, who finished third and missed out. Trailing to an eighth-minute goal by Tyler Dibling, Ireland roared back with two goals from Tommy Lonergan and another from Conor McManus to book their place in the eight-country draw.
